dedupe_keys.name: tsb it migration failure 2018 independent review by slaughter and may

description: This case study is the independent review of the failed migration of TSB Bank's customer accounts to a new IT platform in April 2018, after which customers had problems with online access and large numbers turned to branch and telephone banking, overwhelming contingency resources. The review was carried out by the law firm Slaughter and May for the TSB Board and published on 19 November 2019, with the full report linked as a PDF from TSB's news release. It is free to read. Caveats: the review was commissioned by the bank, so its scope was set by the board, and the release gives only a short summary; regulators' later reports are separate. The review found weaknesses in planning and preparation, including the need for stronger oversight of suppliers, questions about how testing was done, inconsistent configuration of data centres and coding defects that testing missed, and TSB noted that the board had not been told customers could be affected this way. All affected customers were compensated, and TSB took direct control of IT operations and changed its leadership. For simulation it is a documented example of how an IT change can take down a bank's service channels, useful for operational resilience and emergency response studies of digital financial infrastructure. It is related to the Knight Capital trading incident record in this catalogue, another IT failure in finance.
